gloss: thanks to; owing to; because of

definitions.explanation: Used to attribute a good result to someone or something.
Sometimes used ironically to blame someone for a negative outcome.

examples.japanese: あなたのおかげで{助|たす}かりました。
examples.english: I was saved thanks to you.

examples.japanese: おかげさまで{元気|げんき}です。
examples.english: I'm fine, thanks to everyone. (set phrase)

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}のおかげで{合格|ごうかく}できた。
examples.english: I passed thanks to my teacher.

examples.japanese: {君|きみ}のおかげで{遅刻|ちこく}した。
examples.english: I was late because of you. (ironic)

examples.japanese: {薬|くすり}のおかげで{治|なお}った。
examples.english: I got better thanks to the medicine.

examples.japanese: おかげで{無事|ぶじ}に{終|お}わった。
examples.english: Thanks to that, it ended safely.

examples.japanese: あなたのおかげで{大変|たいへん}な{目|め}に{遭|あ}った。
examples.english: Because of you, I had a terrible time.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}のおかげで{試合|しあい}が{中止|ちゅうし}になった。
examples.english: The game was canceled because of the rain.

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}のおかげで{成功|せいこう}した。
examples.english: I succeeded thanks to my efforts.

notes:
おかげ expresses that a result happened 'thanks to' something/someone.

Kanji: Can be written as お{陰|かげ} (shadow/behind the scenes)

Key expression:
- おかげさまで: thanks to you/everyone (very common polite phrase)
  - Used as a response to 'How are you?' or to express general gratitude
  - Shows appreciation without specifying to whom

Grammar pattern:
- 〜のおかげで: thanks to ~, owing to ~

Contrast:
- おかげ (thanks to - usually positive or ironic)
- せい (because of - usually negative/blame): {君|きみ}のせいで... (It's your fault that...)
